We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

Our Fraud team's mission is to help companies detect and prevent fraud using Plaid's financial network data. We believe that transaction patterns, device signals, identity linkages, and behavioral data are dramatically underleveraged tools in fraud prevention. Our products — including Protect and Signal — operate at network scale and depend on real-world investigation and research to stay ahead of adaptive adversaries.

  

As a Fraud Intelligence Analyst, you will sit at the intersection of live fraud investigation, applied data science, and product innovation. You will lead complex investigations, translate findings into detection improvements, and collaborate tightly with Data Science, ML, and Product teams to shape the next generation of Plaid's fraud capabilities. This is not a purely operational role — your research directly drives features, model inputs, and product design.

Live Fraud Investigation & Reconstruction

* Lead investigations into complex fraud cases across identities, accounts, devices, and transaction surfaces

* Reconstruct attacker sequences and hypothesize actor intent and tooling
* Distill patterns from noisy signals into clear narratives and actionable insights
* Bridge investigation outcomes to product and model improvements

Signal & Tool Utilization at Scale

* Operate across Plaid's fraud tooling — dashboards, alerting systems, network signals, and analytics platforms — to detect and validate anomalies
* Stress-test existing capabilities, identify systemic gaps, and define new detection primitives
* Proactively identify gaps in internal fraud tooling and automation, driving enhancements to improve efficiency and scale

Product & Model Partnership

* Collaborate with Data Science, ML/AI, and Product teams to improve labeling, feature sets, evaluation frameworks, and model decay monitoring
* Surface data quality limitations and systematically formalize missing features
* Translate exploratory research into reusable feature pipelines, model inputs, or rule augmentations
* Participate in product discovery, roadmap planning, and post-launch evaluation to ensure fraud-awareness by design

Deep Applied Fraud Research

* Conduct longitudinal and structural analysis of how fraud types manifest in Plaid network data — entity linkages, temporal patterns, attack rotations, tool chains
* Experiment with network/graph analysis, sequence mining, anomaly detection, and custom heuristics where off-the-shelf approaches fail

Ecosystem Monitoring & Knowledge Leadership

* Continuously survey external fraud trends, adversary techniques, tooling, and emerging threat vectors
* Proactively perform threat modeling of abuse surfaces and initiate research proposals when patterns emerge

Case Studies & Reporting

* Produce clear, evidence-backed technical reports and case studies for product, engineering, operations, legal, and executive stakeholders
* Document investigation workflows, attack classifications, and proof-of-concept detection logic
* Drive post-incident learning by capturing lessons from fraud incidents and feeding them back into defenses

* 5+ years of applied fraud experience in a high-velocity environment (fintech, consumer payments, banking, SaaS, marketplace risk, or security research)
* Investigator mindset: pattern synthesis, hypothesis testing, and skilled triage between signal and noise
* End-to-end investigation experience reconstructing attacker intent and behavior in multi-step attack sequences across accounts, devices, and identities
* Post-containment incident response experience with a deep emphasis on post-mortems and root cause analysis
* Dark and grey-web navigation and investigation experience; ability to assess source credibility and translate external intelligence into actionable insights
* Strong communication: ability to explain complex, ambiguous behavior to technical and non-technical audiences
* Tool fluency with data environments and investigative toolchains (BI tools, anomaly detection, case trackers)

Preferred

* Python for scripting, rapid prototyping, and analytical workflows

D’Addario & Company is the largest manufacturer and distributor of musical instrument accessories in the world. As a US based manufacturing company, we pride ourselves on high automation machinery and innovative technology, as well as our commitment to environmentally sustainable practices. Most importantly, we pride ourselves on our diverse team of individuals who embody our core values of curiosity, passion, candor, family, and responsibility and translate them into action every day.

D'Addario is looking for an IT Project Manager to join our Digital Enterprise Systems (DEx) team and lead technology initiatives that support our global business. Judi Health is a health technology company providing benefit administration solutions to employers, unions, health plans, and government entities. Judi Health replaces fragmented, outdated systems with the industry's first Unified Claims Processing™ architecture, seamlessly consolidating pharmacy and medical benefit administration on a single, secure platform. **Position Summary:**

The Government Programs Operations Analyst supports operational functions across Medicare, Medicaid, Exchange, and Commercial lines of business, with the primary responsibility of serving as the Reprocessing & Reversals (R&R) subject matter expert. The Analyst executes and validates R&R activities, provides operational and regulatory guidance, and works closely with Product and Development teams to design, test, and implement system and process enhancements. This role applies expertise in regulatory compliance and claims operations to resolve issues, maintain accurate documentation, and improve the integrity, efficiency, and scalability of operations.

**Position Responsibilities:**

* Serve as the primary Reprocessing & Reversals (R&R) subject matter expert, executing R&R activities and supporting continuous process improvement across applicable lines of business.

* Perform day-to-day operational tasks related to claims processes, including PDE, Medicare Plan Finder, and Encounter Data submissions, while assessing downstream impacts of R&R activities.
* Support error handling and change management for PDE and encounter submissions, ensuring R&R outcomes align with CMS, state, and client requirements.
* Stay current on CMS guidance and regulatory updates, translating changes into actionable operational strategies.
* Share R&R knowledge and provide guidance to team members and cross-functional partners as needed.
* Maintain current knowledge of Medicare & Medicaid requirements to facilitate compliance of ongoing business operations.

**Required Qualifications:**

* 3+ years of experience in PBM or health plan operations, with experience supporting Medicare Part D, Medicaid, Exchange, and/or Commercial
* Proven subject matter expertise in pharmacy claim reprocessing and reversals, including complex claim corrections, operational controls, issue resolution, and downstream regulatory reporting impacts.
* Advanced MS Excel skills (pivot tables, complex formulas, data modeling); familiarity with SQL or other data tools is a plus.
* Demonstrated experience partnering with cross-functional teams to define business requirements, support solution design, perform user acceptance testing, manage defects, and implement operational enhancements.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a track record of driving operational improvements.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with operational and technical stakeholders.
* Deep understanding of CMS compliance requirements and audit readiness.
* Highly organized, detail-oriented, and committed to delivering high-quality work.

*All employees are responsible for adherence to the Judi Health Code of Conduct including the reporting of non-compliance. Our deep curiosity to learn and our eagerness to share diverse passions with others gives us balance and injects a one-of-a-kind vibrancy into our culture.

If you are driven to solve exhilarating challenges and have a bias toward action in the face of change, you will be empowered to make a real impact here, with a sharp and passionate team at your back. If Braze sounds like a place where you can thrive, we can't wait to meet you.

### **The Role**

The best software companies don't grow through direct sales alone. They grow through ecosystems: networks of partners who extend their reach, deepen customer relationships and deliver outcomes no single company can deliver alone. Technology partners sit closest to the product. They are the platforms, data tools and AI services our customers already use, and how well Braze works with them shapes what customers can build.

Technology partnerships at Braze take three forms. Product partnerships are built into the product, where Braze and a partner's technology work together for customers. Strategic partnerships are held at a senior level with a small number of platform companies, including the major cloud and large language model providers. And a long tail of ISVs integrate with Braze and extend what customers can do. Each form has grown on its own terms, and the strategy that connects them is still being written.

This role is key to that strategy. Reporting to the AVP, Partner Experience, you own the strategy, program and plan for technology partnerships in all three forms, and you define it in close collaboration with the VP, Technology Partnerships, who leads the strategic relationships. That means deciding what a technology partner is at Braze, what each type gets from us and what we expect back, and how product, strategic and ISV partnerships fit together, so that partners, Product and the field see one ecosystem rather than three separate efforts. This role owns the strategic and program layer that turns that strategy into something partners and internal teams can actually run on.

You will work closely with Product, the Competitive and Monetization Strategy team, Partner Operations and Business Systems, and alongside the Partner Programs Director, whose tiering, benefits, incentives, portal and directory your program runs within. Several parts of the technology program are ready to be rebuilt, including ISV onboarding and evaluation, co-sell and how competitive situations are handled. We need someone who has built a technology partner program before, to decide what stays, what changes and what goes, and to set a plan for the next 24 months.

Salesforce has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Braze. The agreement has not yet closed and remains subject to customary closing conditions. If it completes, there will be work over the next few years to bring the Braze partner program in line with the broader Salesforce partner program and ecosystem, and this role will play an important part in that.

### **What You'll Own**

* **Technology partnerships strategy, program and plan.** Own the strategy, program and plan for technology partnerships across product, strategic and ISV partners, including partners that have a commercial motion with Braze and partners that do not. Define the strategy in close collaboration with the VP, Technology Partnerships, so it reflects the strategic relationships they lead as well as the ISVs beyond them, and agree the plan with them before it goes wider. Set out what good looks like, in what order, and who needs to do what.
* **What a technology partner is.** Draw the line between an ISV partner, which has an integration with Braze, and a technology partner, which has a commercial motion with Braze. The two overlap, but not every ISV has a commercial motion: some bring value through the product alone and help customers reach specific use cases. Define what each gets from Braze and what Braze expects in return, within the tiering, benefits and incentives set by the Partner Programs Director.
* **Product partnerships.** Bring product partnerships, ISV partnerships and technology partnerships into alignment with Product. Product partnerships are led category by category, so map what exists, agree with the category leads what counts as a partnership, and make sure technology partners have access to, and awareness of, the Product Roadmap.
* **The ISV program.** Following the defined ISV strategy, rebuild the ISV program: how new ISV partners are evaluated, how they are onboarded, and an ideal partner profile (IPP) that tells the team where to invest. Make onboarding something a partner can complete without chasing, and measure how long it takes for a partner to become active.
* **Co-sell and referrals.** Own and scale the co-sell program for technology partners. Take an early trial and turn it into a repeatable program, then run it with other partners: how partners are chosen, how opportunities are shared, how it connects with Sales and what we measure. Design a referral program that works in both directions between Braze and technology partners.
* **Competitive rules of engagement.** Work with the Competitive and Monetization Strategy team to define when a technology partner becomes a competitor and the rules of engagement in those situations. Optimise and scale a universally adopted, ongoing com

jobs.title: Disaster Management & Humanitarian Assistance Research Analyst
jobs.description:
The Disaster Management & Humanitarian Assistance Research Analyst supports the Center for Excellence in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance (CFE-DM) within the Applied Research and Information Sharing (ARIS) program. This position conducts academic research, analysis, and technical writing focused on disaster management and humanitarian assistance, developing operationally relevant publications that strengthen understanding, coordination, and effectiveness across disaster response and humanitarian assistance missions.

The Research Analyst researches and synthesizes complex information to produce high-quality academic and technical products addressing disaster management capabilities, vulnerabilities, and best practices around the world, with particular emphasis on the Pacific Theater. The position requires strong academic research methodologies, advanced writing and editing capabilities, and the ability to translate research findings into practical recommendations for civil-military coordination and humanitarian assistance operations.

Working with subject matter experts, academic institutions, international organizations, and CFE-DM personnel, the Research Analyst contributes to publications, country studies, case studies, training materials, and other information-sharing products that support the Center's mission.

### **Academic Research and Technical Writing**

* Conduct research, analysis, and synthesis of disaster management data and information to produce accurate, comprehensive publications aligned with client-specific style and content requirements, including international civil-military coordination contexts.
* Develop a wide range of disaster management and humanitarian assistance materials, including:

  + Fact sheets, case studies, best practices, research articles, and research studies.
  + Disaster management reference country handbooks.
  + Briefings, presentations, memoranda, information and policy papers, planning documents, and conference materials.
  + Professional journal publications, situation reports, after-action reports, and time-sensitive requests for information (RFIs).
* Apply academic research methodologies to identify, evaluate, and communicate relevant findings.
* Translate research findings into operationally relevant information and practical recommendations for disaster management and humanitarian assistance stakeholders.

### **Case Study Development and Training Support**

* Design and develop operationally relevant disaster response case studies for use in training modules.
* Support civil-military training, exercises, operations, short- and long-term planning, and assessments in alignment with the applicable theater campaign plan through research, information sharing, and the exchange of best practices.

### **Collaboration, Editing, and Quality Assurance**

* Collaborate with subject matter experts (SMEs) to collect and validate information, verify data integrity, and ensure analytic accuracy.
* Facilitate integration of external feedback into documents by reviewing comments, recommending improvements, and ensuring products meet target audience needs.
* Edit research products for logical flow, clarity, completeness, grammar, punctuation, and overall content quality.
* Coordinate with graphics and design staff to ensure drafts meet final production standards for web and print publication.
* Directly support print production and inventory management of information products.

### **Academic Partnerships, Outreach, and Knowledge Sharing**

* Support the Academic Partnership Program by cultivating academic partnerships and facilitating information exchange with universities, students and interns, academic partners, international organizations, and related networks.
* Update data management and information-sharing plans to support program operations.

jobs.title: Insider Threat Investigations Analyst
jobs.description:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

**Job Overview**
================

We are seeking a Insider Threat Investigations Analyst to conduct end to end, from initial triage through case closure. Own investigative fact development, evidence correlation, behavioral risk analysis, and defensible report production. Partner with People, Legal, Cybersecurity, and Physical Security. Add dedicated investigative capacity so referrals are worked promptly and thoroughly as the company scales across multiple sites, including Gulf Coast production. Carry investigations independently, exercise sound judgment on personnel-sensitive matters, and write to a standard that holds up under legal review.

**Responsibilities**
====================

* Conduct insider threat investigations involving data misuse, intellectual property protection concerns, access abuse, fraud indicators, policy violations, and personnel-related security risks. Build investigative plans, timelines, and evidence maps, and manage multiple concurrent investigations through to closure.
* Triage insider threat alerts and referrals, apply threshold criteria, and open investigations when those criteria are met.
* Collect and analyze identity and access logs, data loss prevention events, device and network artifacts, badge and physical access records, People Team inputs, and open-source and internal information. Correlate technical indicators with behavioral indicators and partner with Cybersecurity and digital forensics for deep-dive analysis.
* Preserve evidence and maintain complete, well-organized case files suitable for legal review.
* Coordinate with the People Team and Legal on personnel-sensitive investigative actions. Prepare and deliver concise investigative briefings. Support interview preparation and documentation, and engage with outside counsel or law enforcement when directed.
* Work alongside Risk Intelligence on counterintelligence matters, pairing internal investigative findings with external open-source and public-records collection, and adjudicating both through a single joint intake. Support matters carrying a foreign or external nexus, including undisclosed outside business activity, foreign contact and travel concerns, and attempted targeting or recruitment of Saronic personnel. Escalate to Legal and Security leadership as appropriate.
* Produce clear, objective, and actionable investigative reports and closure summaries that document outcomes, mitigation recommendations, and follow-up requirements. Capture lessons learned and provide case-driven feedback that improves detection quality and reduces false positives.
* Support insider threat program requirements under 32 CFR Part 117, including adverse information reporting and records handling.

**Qualifications**
==================

**Required**

* Bachelor's degree, or equivalent practical experience, in Criminal Justice, Intelligence Studies, Security Management, Cybersecurity, Psychology, or a related field.
* 4+ years of experience in investigations, insider threat, intelligence analysis, security operations, or a related role.
* Demonstrated success handling investigations with personnel and legal implications.
* Strong analytical judgment, disciplined evidence handling, and clear written reporting.
* Ability to handle confidential information and personnel matters with discretion and professionalism.
* Ability to work independently, prioritize competing matters, and carry a case from intake to closure without day-to-day direction.
* Ability to obtain a TS/SCI clearance and to work in controlled or classified environments as required. U.S. Person status required for access to export-controlled information.

**Preferred**

* Experience in insider threat, personnel security, workplace investigations, or corporate internal investigations.
* Familiarity with UEBA, SIEM, DLP, and case management platforms, and with building a timeline from multiple log sources.
* Experience integrating technical evidence with behavioral and open-source investigative inputs.
* Experience supporting investigations across geographically distributed manufacturing or production sites.
* Working knowledge of NISPOM and the National Insider Threat Policy minimum standards.
* Interview support or interview documentation experience.
* Prior defense, Intelligence Community, or cleared industry experience.
* Active TS/SCI clearance.

**Physical Demands**
====================

* Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
* Occasional standing and walking within the office
* Manual dexterity to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other office equipment
* Visual acuity to read screens, documents, and reports

jobs.title: Tech Infra Program Manager, Global Network Deployment (GND)
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.  
  
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.  
  
The successful candidate for this role will create sustainable processes and standards; and drive automation opportunities to reduce delivery cycle times and to improve quality without impacting network availability.  
  
The mission of the team is to deliver network capacity on time with zero rework. The GND Technical Program Manager will support the implementation and delivery of inbound capacity and equipment. They will be responsible for bringing efficiencies in operations and allow the team to scale.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
1. Resolves Planning gaps by driving joint outcomes with stakeholder teams within GND.  
  
2. Owns identifying where systematic issues are blocking planner throughput, driving those to resolution across team boundaries.  
  
3. Collaborates on initiatives within GND that impact Planning (e.g. attend MBRs), and ensures that AMER, EMEA, and APAC regional teams are learning from each other rather than solving the same problems in silos.  
  
4. Provides forward visibility, surfacing risks before they become blockers, engaging the right decision-makers, and driving resolution so planners stay focused on planning and their time is not spent chasing other teams.  
  
5. Ensures solutions are grounded in how planners actually work, translating operational pain points into actionable requirements, representing planning in design discussions, and validating that what ships actually solves the problem.  
  
6. Owns how improvements land in the planning workflow - sequencing rollouts, enabling planners, and confirming that the change actually helps. Drives adoption of tools.  
  
7. Optimizes business processes through Agentic AI solutions.  
  
About the team  
\*Why AWS\*  
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.  
  
\*Diverse Experiences\*  
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.  
  
\*Work/Life Balance\*  
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.  
  
\*Inclusive Team Culture\*  
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.  
  
\*Mentorship and Career Growth\*  
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* 3+ years of technical infrastructure management experience
* Bachelor's degree or equivalent in a related technical field
* Experience in written and verbal communication with the ability to present complex technical information in a clear and concise manner to executives and non-technical leaders
* Experience completing complex tasks quickly with little to no guidance and react with appropriate urgency to situations that require a quick turnaround, or experience prioritizing and handling multiple assignments at any given time while maintaining commitment to deadlines

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

jobs.description:
**Description**

**Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?**

At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainable. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. Our Mission, Vision, and Values guide the way we do business.

***If this sounds like a mission you want to be a part of, keep reading!***

Leidos is seeking an experienced DoWIN Operations Analyst to support the Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) CyberPRIMES program. Leidos is a major partner on the contract and will provide a substantial portion of the cybersecurity workforce supporting the Personnel Readiness Management Agency (PRMA) and DMDC.

The DoDIN Operations Analyst will maintain cyber operational situational awareness, coordinate cybersecurity activities across enterprise stakeholders, track cyber taskings and remediation efforts, support incident response coordination, and prepare operational reporting for leadership. This position serves as the operational bridge between the Security Operations Center (SOC), Cyber Defense teams, Network Operations, System Owners, Risk Management Framework (RMF) stakeholders, and leadership to ensure timely execution of cybersecurity actions and mission requirements across the DMDC enterprise.

  

Work Locations:

Mark Center, Alexandria, Virginia – 1 position

  

**Mission Environment**

DMDC supports the Personnel Readiness Management Agency (PRMA) within the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (OUSD(P&R)) and maintains the Department of Defense’s largest and most comprehensive central repository of personnel, manpower, casualty, pay, entitlement, personnel security, identity, readiness, training, and related data.

  

The PRMA Information Technology (IT) environment includes approximately 15,000 network and endpoint devices supporting more than 600 Government-Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) applications and approximately 100 Risk Management Framework (RMF) authorization boundaries managed through the Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service (eMASS). The DoDIN Operations Analyst operates within the DMDC Cyber Operations environment and supports continuous monitoring, operational coordination, cyber situational awareness, vulnerability management, incident management, and mission assurance activities. The position provides operational oversight and coordination across cybersecurity stakeholders to support the security, availability, and resilience of DMDC systems, networks, and mission-critical services.

  

**Primary Tasks**

* Maintain situational awareness of cybersecurity activity, emerging threats, vulnerabilities, incidents, and operational impacts affecting DMDC systems, applications, and networks.
* Review DoD, Intelligence Community, CISA, vendor, and open-source reporting to identify vulnerabilities, malware, threat activity, and risks relevant to the DMDC environment.
* Analyze cybersecurity operational information to identify trends, recurring issues, operational risks, and potential mission impacts.
* Develop and disseminate situational awareness reports, threat notifications, operational summaries, and executive-level status updates.
* Serve as a coordination point for cybersecurity activities involving SOC analysts, incident responders, cybersecurity engineers, network operations personnel, RMF teams, and system owners.
* Track cybersecurity taskings, incident-response actions, vulnerability-remediation efforts, compliance requirements, and other operational activities through completion.
* Coordinate implementation, validation, mitigation, and reporting of cybersecurity actions across multiple stakeholders.
* Support cyber incident management activities by tracking incidents, coordinating stakeholder communications, and ensuring appropriate escalation procedures are followed.
* Monitor vulnerability remediation activities and support validation of corrective actions across systems and authorization boundaries.
* Assist with management and tracking of Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), cybersecurity findings, and compliance activities.
* Prepare executive-level briefings, dashboards, reports, and decision-support products for leadership.
* Translate technical cybersecurity information into operational impacts, risk assessments, and recommended courses of action for technical and non-technical audiences.
* Coordinate stakeholder communications during significant cybersecurity events, operational disruptions, and incident-response activities.
* Support cybersecurity assessments, inspections, audits, and reporting requirements.
* Contribute to process improvements, operational procedures, reporting workflows, and coordination activities to enhance mission effectiveness.
Maintain complete and accurate records of cybersecurity operational activities, task status, risk information, and supporting documentation in Government-approved systems.  

  

**Basic Qualifications**

* BS degree or equivalent and 2-6 years of prior relevant experience, or a Master's degree with less experience, in cybersecurity operations, network operations, cyber defense, information assurance, or related fields.
* Experience supporting cybersecurity operations, cyber defense, incident management, vulnerability management, or continuous monitoring activities.
* Experience coordinating activities among multiple technical and operational stakeholders.
* Experience developing operational reports, executive briefings, dashboards, or cybersecurity status updates.
* Experience tracking cybersecurity taskings, remediation efforts, corrective actions, or compliance activities.
* Working knowledge of cybersecurity operations, Computer Network Defense (CND), incident-response processes, and threat management principles.

jobs.description:
The Institute for Defense Analyses (IDA) is seeking an experienced Research Analyst to join the Science, Systems, and Sustainment Division (S3D).

This role is for a researcher who is able to contribute to ongoing projects involving the technical details of satellite survivability and higher order effects on military operations and planning. Modeling and simulation experience is needed, plus the ability to derive actionable recommendations for government leaders, communicated in a clear manner. You will participate in and lead technically rigorous studies, develop new analytic approaches, and translate complex results into defensible insights for senior decision-makers.

Specific research-related activities expected of this position include:

Responsibilities

* Develop and maintain relationships with potential sponsors and stakeholders in the national security community to identify emerging issues.
* Engage effectively with sponsors to understand their issues and constraints, and develop responsive research plans.
* Independently formulate research questions that address sponsors’ challenging and complex problems, and are informed by the broader context of national security.
* Identify key factors of the issue under study, and create and execute appropriate quantitative analytic methodologies, including novel computational and model-based approaches.
* Interact with government officials, military personnel, and other subject matter experts during the research process.
* Analyze, evaluate, and integrate data and model results with operational plans to understand impacts on the warfighter.
* Prepare reports and presentations documenting findings, conclusions, and recommendations and effectively communicate the results of IDA’s analysis to sponsors and selected audiences.

Required Qualifications

* Ph.D. in Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, or a closely related quantitative field with at least 3 years of relevant experience beyond academic work (e.g. industry, government, national lab, or other professional setting), or
* Master’s degree in one of the above fields with at least 8 years of relevant experience beyond academic work.
* Ability to work independently and collaboratively in small, high-performing, research teams.
* Strong technical communication skills, particularly the ability to communicate technical information to technical and non-technical audiences, including IDA collaborators and project leaders.
* Space Systems experience is desirable but not a requirement
* Significant interest in Department of War issues and military operations.
* Successful completion of a criminal background check is required.
* Travel (domestic or international) may be required.
* Ability to obtain and maintain a TS/SCI level security clearance. Having a current TS/SCI clearance is strongly desired.

The Research Environment

IDA research staff work on problems that do not have predefined solutions. Successful analysts are:

* Self-directed and intellectually curious.
* Comfortable working across disciplines.
* Able to contribute to multiple concurrent studies.
* Motivated by quantitative, high-consequence, analysis.

You will work with peers who value methodological rigor, independence of thought, and technical excellence.

**Why work at IDA?**

IDA, as a non-profit, is uniquely positioned to answer the most challenging U.S. security and science questions with objective and rigorous analysis leveraging extraordinary scientific, technical, and analytic expertise. This position is located in Alexandria, VA, just outside Washington, D.C.

IDA takes great pride in the high caliber and timeliness of its analyses, which are produced in a collegial atmosphere that encourages independent thinking, teamwork, and objective results. IDA provides an inclusive work environment and a comprehensive and competitive salary and benefits package.

What are the next steps?

* Complete the application and submit your resume.
* The application process consists of three interviews.

  + A short screening call with HR;
  + A 30 min – 60 min screening call with researchers; and
  + Full day interview with various researchers and staff; includes giving a presentation on a research project.

Prior to the full day interview, you will be asked to provide:

* Transcripts (unofficial accepted);
* 3 letters of recommendation; and
* A writing sample.

At IDA, we pride ourselves on offering a comprehensive benefits package that ensures the well-being and security of our staff and their families. We provide a range of medical plans as well as stand-alone dental and vision coverage. Our retirement plans are designed to secure the financial future of our staff, featuring a generous contribution of 10% of base salary to our Qualified Retirement Plan after six months of service. We are committed to promoting a healthy work-life balance with a flexible work environment, an Employee Assistance Plan, paid parental leave, 10 paid holidays, and generous paid time off. IDA encourages professional development and offers tuition reimbursement and other learning opportunities. Learn more about our robust benefit offerings here.

**Pay**

**General Information**

The Office of the State Superintendent of Education (OSSE) is the State Education Agency for the District of Columbia charged with raising the quality of education for all DC residents. OSSE is focused on sustaining, accelerating, and deepening the progress being made for the District’s 90,000+ students. OSSE serves as the District’s liaison to the U.S. Department of Education and works closely with the District’s 470+ early childhood facilities, 250+ schools, 60+ local education agencies (including DCPS and charter organizations), and community-based organizations to provide critical programming and resources to our stakeholders. This position is located in the Office of the State Superintendent of Education (OSSE), Division of Teaching and Learning. The Division of Teaching and Learning is tasked with providing training and technical assistance and professional development for educators across the District. The Division supports OSSE’s mission that all DC students, from infants through adult learners have access to high-quality education and can learn and achieve at high levels.

The Comprehensive Literacy State Development (CLSD) Grant Specialist will be responsible for managing aspects of the administration and implementation of the CLSD grant, a 5-year, $50 million grant awarded to OSSE in Sept. 2024 by the U.S. Department of Education.Support a federal grant program with technical assistance to grantees, including providing ongoing strategic support for grant implementation and grant routines, including reimbursement and monitoring, as well as managing grantee data and reporting for the District of Columbia.

Job description

**Please note:** This is a full-time **shift-based role**, requiring you to work a rotating pattern of early, late and night shifts, including weekends. Your shift pattern will be fixed. While flexibility around shifts may be limited, we'll work with you wherever possible to support a healthy work-life balance and take account of responsibilities outside of work. Further information about the shift pattern will be shared with successful candidates.

**Flexible working:** Due to the nature of this role, flexible, home or remote working isn’t possible.

**About us**

MI5keeps the country safe from serious threats like terrorism and attempts by states to harm the UK, its people and way of life. We carry out investigations by obtaining, analysing and assessing intelligence, and then work with a range of partners, including MI6 and GCHQ to disrupt these threats. Through our protective security arm, we provide advice and guidance to government, businesses and other organisations about how to keep themselves safe. A role in MI5 means you’ll do unique and challenging work in a supportive and encouraging environment, making a real difference to UK national security.

**The role**  
Those who seek to harm the UK don’t work 9am to 5pm, so neither do we. Intelligence Operations Analysts gather information and provide a rapid response to operational teams working around the clock. We analyse data to identify serious and often hidden threats. You’ll work closely with colleagues across MI5 to understand their requirements and learn how to use our tools and techniques to assess a range of intelligence, including audio files, images and written communications, large data sets and location data.

The intelligence gathered doesn’t always reveal the full story. You’ll help unlock the details to determine what’s happening right now, whether it’s cause for concern, and what could happen next. You’ll analyse information as it becomes available from a range of sources, identify patterns and anomalies, and share your findings clearly and accurately to support operational decision-making.

Whether you’re on an early, late or night shift, you’ll be supporting live activity rather than building a picture over weeks or months, helping teams make decisions in the moment. And you won’t be doing it alone. The nature of the shifts and the importance of the work means we share a common goal and a real sense of camaraderie and team support. This is a role with real impact; the insight and connections you and your team provide could lead to major turning points in live investigations.

You’ll receive regular days off throughout your shift cycle, including extended periods away from work, plus dedicated personal development time. **Please note, you’ll need to be able to commute to West London and be ready to start work promptly for early shifts**.

**About you**

You might be a final year undergraduate or a recent graduate, returning to work after a break, looking for a career change or simply a new challenge. To apply, you'll have, or be expected to obtain by September 2027, a 2:2 degree or above in any subject **or** at least one year's full-time work experience using the core skills needed for analysis. Specific analyst experience isn’t required, but you should be able to demonstrate an ability to analyse information, data, evidence or trends. This may have come from your studies, work or everyday life.

Importantly, you’ll have an interest in innovation and enjoy solving problems and puzzles, or finding out what makes things work. So, you’ll be curious; someone who forms conclusions based on evidence. Resilience is key; you’ll be comfortable working at pace and under pressure as you’ll be supporting live activity as it unfolds. You might not always get the right answer from what you’re analysing, so you’ll stay focused, patient and adapt to changing demands and intricate problems as required.

Collaboration is critical. You might be understanding unique requirements, communicating complex analytics to non-technical colleagues, writing handover notes at the end of your shift, or presenting your findings. You’ll be clear and to-the-point, especially when working on something time-sensitive. At all times, you’ll combine attention to detail with sound judgement in time-critical scenarios.

Please note that there is a hearing test as part of the application process. This is because the role will involve listening to audio files. If you wear hearing aids, you’ll be able to complete the test using them.

To perform roles effectively across MI5, employees need to be able to understand information provided in English, including emails, workplace communications and other work-related documents; communicate in English as part of meetings and discussions; and produce and respond to written communications in English relevant to their role.

During training, you’ll work standard Monday to Friday office hours, while developing the skills, techniques and confidence needed for the role. Shift and weekend allowances begin once training has been successfully completed.

jobs.title: Senior Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
PGI is a global consultancy that helps organisations build digital resilience. We deploy our people to implement solutions on behalf of clients or to support them in developing their own capabilities. Our vision is a world resilient to digital threats and online harm. To achieve this, we need to grow our team of talented and passionate people. Our clients include some of the most well-known global brands, national governments, and innovative growing businesses. We operate in an exciting, fast-growing sector that bears increasing relevance and importance to nation-states, corporates, universities, and NGOs.

#### **What you'll be doing**

PGI’s threat intelligence functions continue to expand, driving our successful growth. As a Senior Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Analyst, you will track threat actors, campaigns and criminal ecosystems, and turn findings into actionable intelligence for clients. The responsibilities of the post are as follows:

* Lead CTI engagements, owning analytic direction and output quality, and acting as senior analytical point of contact for clients.
* Produce strategic and tactical CTI products, from executive-level assessments that draw together cyber, physical and geopolitical indicators to actor profiles, threat landscapes and alerts, tailored to each client’s requirements.
* Monitor and research threat actors, including ransomware and extortion groups, initial access brokers, hacktivists and state-linked actors.
* Collect, enrich and pivot on technical indicators to attribute activity and uncover wider campaigns.
* Identify client exposure, including leaked credentials, breaches, brand impersonation, lookalike domains and attack surface weaknesses, escalating urgent issues promptly.
* Work with clients to define and refine priority intelligence requirements (PIRs), and present findings to technical and non-technical audiences.
* Apply rigorous analytic standards: source evaluation, confidence language and clear separation of fact, assessment and judgement, and act as a peer reviewer for other analysts’ work through our QA process.
* Build and improve our collection, enrichment and threat actor tracking tools and workflows, including responsible use of AI for tasks.
* Design and deliver table-top exercises and training that take clients through realistic threat scenarios.
* Mentor junior analysts, sharing tradecraft and raising analytic standards.
* Contribute to proposals and thought leadership.

#### **One day one you will bring**

* At least five years’ experience in cyber threat intelligence or threat research, ideally in a consultancy, government, intelligence or security vendor environment, including leading projects and mentoring or reviewing other analysts’ work.
* Deep understanding of the threat landscape, including attack techniques, the cybercrime economy, state-linked activity and emerging AI-enabled threats such as deepfake and identity fraud.
* Excellent written English, with experience producing concise, well-evidenced assessments for both technical and executive audiences.
* Ability to build or automate collection and enrichment tooling (e.g. Python), and familiarity with CTI platforms and indicator analysis.
* Experience researching safely in dark web and closed-source environments, with sound OPSEC and discretion with sensitive information.
* Working knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK and structured analytic techniques, and the ability to express confidence and uncertainty clearly.
* Desirable: experience designing and delivering training or table-top exercises; disinformation or influence operations analysis; malware or blockchain analysis; relevant certifications (e.g. GCTI, CREST CPTIA, OSIP); additional languages relevant to the threat landscape.
* Eligible for SC clearance and willing to undergo vetting.

**Diversity, Equity and Inclusion at PGI**

As a British company which operates internationally, we draw strength from the diversity of our people. Without our diverse team, we couldn’t do the work we do. We are involved in projects across 80+ geographies, our people speak 25+ languages and come from a variety of backgrounds. By hiring and cultivating a diverse, equitable and inclusive workforce, we can uphold values that enable every member of the team to thrive, while delivering novel solutions to novel problems.

**Accessibility at PGI**

Every individual has different requirements, so we are committed to implementing reasonable adjustments to mitigate physical and non-physical barriers in the workplace.

We strive to make the recruitment process as accessible as possible, but if you have any questions or concerns, please get in touch.

***Please note:*** *We are not accepting applications or speculative profiles from any recruitment agencies. If we require additional resource, we will reach out to you.*

jobs.title: Senior Deployment Strategist
jobs.description:
**About Euphoric**
------------------

Euphoric builds AI-first employee benefits administration software for the world's largest and most prestigious employers. We spun out of Peppy Health to take on what we believe is the biggest untouched opportunity in enterprise software.

Global employers spend $3–5 trillion on benefits every year. It is their second-largest cost after payroll, yet the category still runs on legacy systems and spreadsheets. Incumbents cannot move fast enough, and AI-first startups have mostly overlooked it.

We have two products:

* **GAP (Global Administration Platform)** for global benefits teams. It uses LLMs to parse and extract policy documents into a structured ontology, and gives admins spend and utilisation tools across every country they operate in.
* **Navigator**, the employee-facing product that helps people understand and use their benefits.

We are post product-market fit at seed stage, live with some of the world's largest household-name enterprises, and we land and expand country by country. Our big current focus is flexible benefits and open enrollment. We stay deliberately lean so that the people who join own a meaningful piece of what we build.

This is also genuine tech for good: better benefits administration directly improves the wellbeing and financial security of millions of employees.

**The Role**

As a **Senior** **Deployment Strategist** you will spend roughly 80% of your time on client work and 20% on developing our products. You will own a portfolio of approximately 1 to 3 enterprise accounts, depending on size, from post-sale through live launch and beyond.

This is not a project management role. With the Euphoric MCP you will build custom agents, automations and workflows for some of the world's largest employers. You will be on the edge of AI in the workplace, guiding how global enterprises roll AI out to their benefits teams and employees.

**What You’ll Do:**
-------------------

No two weeks are the same as a **Senior** **Deployment Strategist**, but you can expect to:

* **Own your accounts end to end.** Be the named owner for approximately 1 to 3 enterprise clients, depending on size, from post-sale handover through implementation, live launch, renewal and expansion into new countries.
* **Drive land and expand.** Configure demos and the actual product for potential expansions, from new countries to new employee populations, so clients see working product, not slides.
* **Deliver deployments.** Configure GAP and Navigator for each client, build implementation plans, run UAT, manage data and policy-document onboarding, handle support and track adoption on live data.
* **Go on site.** Spend real time with clients' benefits and HR teams, including regional rollouts and country launches. On average expect around 1 day a week on client site; it varies, with heavier weeks around launches and occasional international travel as our clients expand globally.
* **Lead workshops and train clients.** Run discovery and design workshops, and train client teams so they get full value from GAP and Navigator.
* **Build with the Euphoric MCP.** Design and ship custom agents, automations and workflows that solve each client's specific problems, from reporting and renewals to employee communications.
* **Run the relationship.** Be the day-to-day contact, write clear client emails, and build the decks, QBRs and proposals that move senior stakeholders, from benefits administrators up to global heads of reward.
* **Shape the product (~20%).** Work closely with core product, engineering and design to build out specific features and flows your accounts need. Bring field insight back so it becomes part of the core platform.
* **Step into product when it's quieter.** In weeks where client work is less intense, you are fully expected to support in a product capacity: specs, evals, prompts, testing and analytics.
* **Work hand in hand with Deployed Product Managers.** They will join you on site to learn how to improve the core product. You will own the client-specific work.

**Skills & Experience**
-----------------------

**About us**

MI5keeps the country safe from serious threats like terrorism and attempts by states to harm the UK, its people and way of life. We carry out investigations by obtaining, analysing and assessing intelligence, and then work with a range of partners, including MI6 and GCHQ to disrupt these threats. Through our protective security arm, we provide advice and guidance to government, businesses and other organisations about how to keep themselves safe. A role in MI5 means youll do unique and challenging work in a supportive and encouraging environment, making a real difference to UK national security.

Those who seek to do us harm dont work 9am to 5pm, so neither do we. We analyse data to identify serious and often hidden threats. Youll work closely with colleagues across MI5 to understand their requirements and learn how to use our tools and techniques to assess a range of intelligence, including audio files, images and written communications, large data sets and location data.

  

The intelligence gathered doesnt always reveal the full story. Youll help unlock the details to determine whats happening right now, whether its cause for concern, and what could happen next. Youll analyse information as it becomes available from a range of sources, identify patterns and anomalies, and share your findings clearly and accurately to support operational decision-making.

  

Whether youre on an early, late or night shift, youll be supporting live activity rather than building a picture over weeks or months, helping teams make decisions in the moment. And you wont be doing it alone. The nature of the shifts and the importance of the work means we share a common goal and a real sense of camaraderie and team support. This is a role with real impact; the insight and connections you and your team provide could lead to major turning points in live investigations.

  

Youll receive regular days off throughout your shift cycle, including extended periods away from work, plus dedicated personal development time. **Please note, youll need to be able to commute to West London and be ready to start work promptly for early shifts**.

### **Person specification**

**About you**

You might be a final year undergraduate or a recent graduate, returning to work after a break, looking for a career change or simply a new challenge. Specific analyst experience isnt required, but you should be able to demonstrate an ability to analyse information, data, evidence or trends. Importantly, youll enjoy solving problems and puzzles, or finding out what makes things work. So, youll be curious; someone who forms conclusions based on evidence. Resilience is key; youll be comfortable working at pace and under pressure as youll be supporting live activity as it unfolds. You might not always get the right answer from what youre analysing, so youll stay focused, patient and adapt to changing demands and intricate problems as required.

  

Collaboration is critical. ### **Job description**

The role of Data Analysts in the DWP AC is built around the ability to understand, manipulate, accurately analyse and communicate insight from data.

Data Analysts apply a range of techniques such as statistical analysis and time series forecasting using a range of analytical and data visualisation tools e.g. SAS, SQL, R, advanced Excel, Qlik. jobs.title: Information Security Analyst
jobs.description:
**Job Overview**

Based within the Information Security team, the Information Security Analyst will be working closely with the Head of Information Security, the delivery team and key business stakeholders. This role combines information security and GRC consultancy with hands-on configuration and implementation of the OneTrust platform.

This role will be involved in:

* Implementing and supporting IT Risk Management and Third Party Risk Management projects using OneTrust.
* Supporting clients with ISO 27001 ISMS implementation and compliance services.
* Providing practical information security, risk and GRC advice to clients.
* Undertaking multiple projects in all areas of information management including information security, data protection and information governance.

**Responsibilities**

**Client Delivery**

* Support the delivery of client information security, GRC, IT Risk Management and Third Party Risk Management engagements.
* Configure and implement OneTrust GRC solutions to meet client requirements, including assessments, attributes, workflows and related platform functionality.
* Support clients with the implementation and ongoing operation of ISO 27001 Information Security Management Systems (ISMS).
* Listen to and understand client issues, translate requirements into practical solutions and provide clear recommendations.
* Deliver training, presentations and education on information security topics and the OneTrust platform.

**Risk, Assurance and Compliance**

* Support clients with IT risk and third-party risk management, including the identification, assessment, documentation and treatment of information security and cyber risks.
* Review and risk assess client suppliers as part of managed services, evaluating security posture and supporting decisions on remediation, risk acceptance or supplier rejection.
* Support clients in developing, implementing and maintaining information security policies, controls and procedures.
* Carry out and document appropriate ISMS reviews, audits and spot checks to assess whether policies, controls and procedures are operating effectively.
* Support clients in understanding and responding to relevant information security regulatory and compliance requirements, including DORA where applicable.
* Maintain appropriate records and evidence to demonstrate compliance with relevant standards, regulatory requirements and good practice.

**Client and Stakeholder Relationships**

* Build effective working relationships with client stakeholders, internal teams and third-party suppliers.
* Communicate complex security, risk and regulatory requirements clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
* Work confidently with senior stakeholders, constructively challenge where required and support informed decision-making.
* Manage multiple pieces of work at the same time, maintaining quality and prioritising effectively.

**Internal Information Security**

* Maintain Oyster IMS Policy Management processes through OneTrust, including monitoring policy publication and attestation.
* Administer and support the Phished platform in partnership with the internal Support Team, including phishing simulations, awareness activity and testing of internal processes.
* Support the ongoing effectiveness and continuous improvement of Oyster IMS information security processes and controls.
* Maintain relevant OneTrust learning and certifications and keep technical knowledge current.

**Who we're looking for**

**Essential**

* Around three to five years' relevant experience in information security, GRC, IT risk, third-party risk management, data protection or a related discipline.
* Ability to translate business requirements into solutions and deliver for clients
* Practical, hands-on experience using OneTrust (or similar tools) GRC, ideally including the creation or configuration of assessments, attributes and workflows.
* Practical experience supporting information security risk assessments, supplier assurance or third-party risk management activities.
* Experience applying information security policies, controls and risk management practices within an organisation.
* Able to explain complex security, risk and regulatory requirements clearly and practically.
* Confident working with senior stakeholders and able to influence decisions appropriately.
* Strong problem-solving skills with the judgement to propose proportionate, workable solutions.
* Collaborative and able to work effectively with individuals and teams on both planned and ad-hoc activities.
* Resilient and comfortable challenging assumptions or decisions constructively when required.
* Well organised, able to manage competing priorities and committed to delivering high-quality work.

**Desirable**

* Experience configuring OneTrust Third Party Risk Management, IT Risk Management, Compliance Automation and/or Enterprise Policy Management modules.
* Practical experience applying DORA or comparable regulatory requirements within a client or organisational environment.
* Experience supporting ISO 27001 ISMS implementation, operation or compliance activities.
* Recent and relevant OneTrust certification(s), or equivalent evidence of current OneTrust capability.

Pay: £45,000.00-£60,000.00 per year

* Enhanced paternity leave

jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Amazon buys from hundreds of thousands of suppliers worldwide. Do you want to build one trusted view of who they are, and make that data ready for AI to reason and act on at global scale? As a Technical Program Manager on the Global Procurement Technology team, you will lead the supplier data programs at the center of Amazon's procurement AI transformation. You will drive the Supplier Mapping Framework, an AI-powered entity-resolution platform that unifies supplier identities and spend across systems. You will also drive Supplier 360, the supplier profile and search experience that procurement teams and AI applications across Amazon rely on.  
  
You will own roadmaps and delivery end to end. That means turning ambiguous business problems into clear requirements, setting data-quality and governance mechanisms, and aligning upstream data owners and downstream consumers across organizations. You will partner with software engineers, data engineers, scientists, business intelligence engineers and business stakeholders to launch reliable data products that shape sourcing, risk and spend decisions worldwide. If you enjoy driving clarity through ambiguity and want your programs to influence procurement strategy globally, we want to hear from you.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Own the end-to-end roadmap, requirements and delivery for the Supplier Mapping Framework and Supplier 360, from problem definition through launch and adoption.
* Turn ambiguous business needs from category management, sourcing, supplier risk and audit teams into clear requirements, phased plans and measurable success metrics.
* Drive data-quality and governance mechanisms, such as match accuracy, coverage reporting and source-of-truth validation, so supplier data can be trusted for decisions and AI applications.
* Align upstream data owners and downstream consumers across organizations on dependencies, data access, compliance requirements and launch timelines.
* Lead operational excellence for production data and AI systems, including launch readiness, metrics reviews, incident follow-up and continuous improvement.

  
A day in the life  
Your day balances collaboration with focused time, and you'll work with engineering teams and stakeholders across time zones. You might start by reviewing match-accuracy and data-quality metrics for the Supplier Mapping Framework. Then you might sync with engineers on a launch dependency, or work through a requirements question with a supplier risk or audit partner. You'll join sprint ceremonies with your squad, walk through designs with engineers and scientists, and align with product managers and business leaders on priorities for Supplier 360. In your focused hours, you might write a requirements document, build a phased delivery plan, prepare a metrics or business review, or dig into an operational issue with the engineering team to settle root cause and next steps. The rhythm gives you regular cross-time-zone collaboration balanced with dedicated heads-down hours each day.  
  
About the team  
Global Procurement Technology sits within Global Procurement Operations and builds the data and technology products that power Amazon's procurement processes worldwide. Our key products include the supplier mapping framework, the trusted supplier data repository, and the supplier management system. The team is an agile group of data engineers, software engineers, scientists, and product and program managers, with Principal Engineers in the broader organization providing technical guidance. You will have the chance to build skills across engineering disciplines, and the team's collaborative setup means you can grow by contributing to software, data, and AI work alike.

------------------------

* 3+ years of technical product or program management experience
* 2+ years of software development experience
* 3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
* Experience managing technical programs across cross-functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
* Experience developing and executing/delivering product and technical roadmaps
* Bachelor's degree

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* 3+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
* Experience building and evaluating system-level technical design
* Experience with roadmap strategy and definition

jobs.title: Financial Data Analyst
jobs.description:
**ABOUT CIM GROUP:**

CIM is a community-focused real estate and infrastructure owner, operator, lender, and developer. Our team of experts works together to identify and create value in real assets, benefiting the communities in which we invest. Back in 1994, our three founders focused on projects in Southern California neighborhoods. Today, we are a diverse team of 900+ employees with projects across the Americas. Our projects have delivered jobs; created comfortable places to live, work, and relax; and provided necessary and sustainable infrastructure. Our focus on enhancing communities is unwavering, and we strive to make an even greater impact in the years to come. Join us and make an impact today!

**POSITION PURPOSE:**

The Financial Data Analyst owns the ongoing integrity of the financial and performance data CIM relies on for investor reporting, internal decision-making, and business planning. To start, the scope of data for this position will include investment performance across CIM’s funds, separately managed accounts, and co-investment vehicles, and will extend over time to other financial analytics such as FP&A, forecasting, and fund accounting outputs. Metrics are produced through automated processes; the Financial Data Analyst is accountable for every reporting cycle’s controls that keep them accurate. This role will continuously improve control coverage and automation as funds, methodologies, and the data platform evolve. The Financial Data Analyst owns validation logic and control operation and will partner closely with Data Engineering as the primary owners of pipeline infrastructure. This is a hands-on, analytical and technical role for someone with expertise in financial and performance data in alternative investments and an explicit interest in leading ongoing governance and controls.

### **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Data Validation & Continuous Control Improvement**

* Own automated validation of performance metrics (IRR, TWR, MOIC, DPI, RVPI, TVPI) across funds, SMAs, and co-investment vehicles, running and monitoring controls every reporting cycle.
* Extend the control framework to additional financial analytics — including budgets, forecasts, cash projections, and fund accounting outputs.
* Maintain validation rules and tolerances — reasonableness checks, variance thresholds, cross-metric consistency (for example, DPI + RVPI = TVPI), and independent recalculation — and recalibrate them as exception patterns and structures change.
* Operate automated reconciliations to NAV, general ledger, and capital accounts; manage exceptions to resolution and fix the root causes of recurring issues.
* Track control performance — exception rates, false positives, resolution time, and automation coverage — and use it to prioritize ongoing improvements.
* Maintain data lineage from reported figures to source systems.
* Apply documented performance methodologies as testable logic, and propose a recommended treatment for edge cases (such as DPI netting, broken deals, and recycled capital) for the methodology owner’s decision.
* Perform variance analysis and attribution, and explain the drivers of results in clear, documented narratives.

**Governance & Controls**

* Run governance and control routines each reporting cycle, test their effectiveness periodically, and refine control design based on the results.
* Maintain a living control inventory — what is checked, how often, and who is accountable — with supporting evidence.
* Contribute to the Track Record Policy Change Operating Process, and update validation rules and regression tests for each approved change.
* Work with Data Engineering on pipeline enhancements, test coverage, and release controls.
* Partner with Compliance and Legal to support regulatory requirements for track record presentations, including the SEC Marketing Rule.
* Maintain audit-ready documentation for internal reviews, external audits, DDQ responses, and LP inquiries.

**Financial Analysis & Reporting Support**

* Provide the financial analysis behind investor reporting and DDQ responses, keeping figures and disclosures consistent across materials.
* Maintain analytical models, reconciliations, and templates, and convert manual, repetitive steps into controlled, repeatable processes.
* Partner with Fund Accounting, FP&A, Portfolio Oversight, Investments, and Investor Relations to resolve discrepancies and align reported figures.

### **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* 3–6 years in performance measurement, fund accounting, FP&A, investment analytics, controls, or financial analysis. Experience in alternative investments is strongly preferred.
* Working knowledge of performance metrics and methodologies, including IRR, TWR, MOIC, DPI, RVPI, TVPI, and attribution.
* Proficiency in SQL for querying source data, reconciling outputs, and building automated validation checks.
* Experience operating and improving automated reconciliation, data quality, or controls frameworks, or testing financial calculations.
* Demonstrated ability to own a recurring reporting cycle (such as quarter-close) alongside a standing improvement backlog.
* Strong financial analysis skills and advanced Excel.
* Attention to detail, a skeptical mindset, and clear communication — including explaining why a number moved.

### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Python or PySpark for validation logic; Databricks or a comparable lakehouse platform; Domo or another BI tool for control reporting.
* Familiarity with version control, code review, and automated testing.
* Alternatives, real estate, or infrastructure asset management experience, including quarter-close and investor-reporting cycles.
* Exposure to FP&A, forecasting, or budgeting processes.
* Familiarity with GIPS, NCREIF / PREA, INREV, ILPA, the SEC Marketing Rule, and DDQ processes.
* CFA Level I or II passed, or the CAIA designation (in progress or completed).

### **EDUCATION:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics
